newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE supports OPEC efforts to stabilise oil market.
newsitem.headline: UAE supports OPEC efforts to stabilise oil market.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates told OPEC on Tuesday it supported its efforts to find a way to help boost oil prices and stabilise world markets, the official news agency WAM said.

UAE Petroleum and Mineral Resources Minister Obaid bin Saif al-Nasseri also told OPEC President Abdullah Salem al-Badri that the UAE was committed to its supply quota of 2.161 million barrels per day (bpd), it added.

In a meeting with Badri, who is also Libya's oil minister, Nasseri urged other members in the 11-nation cartel to adhere to production quotas set by OPEC ahead of the group's next ministerial meeting in Vienna in June.

Badri told WAM that "consultations were underway among OPEC members to crystalise a definitive formula to help the June meeting realise a commitment to quotas and achieve stability in world markets to boost oil prices."

He is touring the region to brief Gulf Arab oil producers on the outcome of last week's meeting in Isfahan of an OPEC quota compliance committee. Badri has said he believed that most OPEC members would favour sticking to their current production ceiling at their June meeting.
The UAE derives about 75 percent of government revenue from oil. It is one of few oil producers with spare production capacity and sufficient reserves of crude oil to last a century.
Badri, who has been to Qatar, is expected to leave for Saudi Arabia later in the day.
